messages.author: f4c2e63aec3c6db2
messages.subject: new Python MCMC package, sampyl
parts:
Just saw this one. My sense is that what is going on here is that people
want to combine Gibbs with other samplers (e.g. NUTS) at various points
and being able to do everything in Python is really nice. (I may be
wrong about this though.)

-------------------------------------

Sampyl

July 1, 2015: version 0.2

Sampyl is a package for sampling from probability distributions using
MCMC methods. Similar to PyMC3 using theano to compute gradients, Sampyl
uses autograd to compute gradients. However, you are free to write your
own gradient functions, autograd is not necessary. This project was
started as a way to use MCMC samplers by defining models purely with
Python and numpy.

https://github.com/mcleonard/sampyl

Sampyl includes three samplers currently:

Metropolis-Hastings
Hamiltonian
NUTS


autograd = https://github.com/HIPS/autograd

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] new Python MCMC package, sampyl
parts:
> On Jul 2, 2015, at 8:46 AM, Allen B. Riddell <a...@ariddell.org> wrote:
>
> Just saw this one. My sense is that what is going on here is that people
> want to combine Gibbs with other samplers (e.g. NUTS) at various points
> and being able to do everything in Python is really nice. (I may be
> wrong about this though.)

I agree.

Especially about the "do everything in Python" part.

Of course, you still need to learn how to express the model
or how to constrain yourself to the bits of the language
they can autodiff.

One possibility for PyStan (and RStan and Stan.jl and ...)
would be to have an object-oriented way to specify either
graphical models or log density expressions in language that was in
language, but then converted to Stan and ran in Stan on the
back end. Then Stan would look like PyMC3 from a Python
user's perspective --- that is, no domain-specific language
syntax to learn, just an object or expression structure within
Python.

I wish I had time to follow up on all of these packages.

Any idea what they're all doing for constrained parameters?

- Bob
